title: VPN audit schema and approval sandbox notes
summary: Working draft capturing a minimal, testable audit-log schema for customer-managed VPNs plus an approval-sandbox recipe that operators can run locally. Goal: define a compact evidence shape that satisfies enterprise audit requirements while keeping payload size small for low-bandwidth customer links.
background: Customers deploying Redwood Private sometimes front the inference control plane with customer-managed VPNs / IPsec connectors. We need consistent audit trails and approval gates for any VPC-level changes (peer up/down, route edits, NAT policy changes) that are both legally defensible and network-bandwidth conscious. Current product notes are heavy on attestation UX but less prescriptive on log shape and sampling for VPN scenarios.
goals: 1) Produce a small, unambiguous audit record for VPN control-plane events. 2) Define operator sandbox steps to reproduce approval gating in staging. 3) Provide sampling/retention guidance for customers with constrained egress. 4) Provide a verification primitive that SRE/CS can use during onboarding.
non_goals: Do not attempt to fully standardize telemetry format across all connectivity types (we focus on VPN/overlay for this doc). This is not the final legal contract for enterprise audits — it is a product/engineering playbook that maps to compliance needs.
acceptance_criteria:
- A minimal schema doc that maps to customer audit requirements (identity, action, before/after snapshot, evidence link).
- A small runnable sandbox recipe (steps + sample logs) that an operator can follow to reproduce an approval + log capture.
- A recommended retention tiering: 7d hot, 90d warm, 2y cold (configurable).
audit_log_schema:
Proposed compact schema (newline-delimited JSON events). Keep fields stable and avoid heavy binary payloads. Field list: event_id, timestamp_utc, actor_id (email or service-principal), actor_role, action_type (route_create/route_delete/peer_establish/peer_teardown/nat_change), target_resource (vpc-id|peer-id), before_sha256 (optional compact diff hash), after_sha256 (optional compact diff hash), evidence_refs (list of signed URIs), operator_assertion (signed short string), sampling_bucket (low|medium|full), truncated (bool), retention_class (hot|warm|cold). Example event (single line):
{
  "event_id": "evt-20250910-7f2a",
  "timestamp_utc": "2025-09-10T18:12:07Z",
  "actor_id": "ops+alice@customer.com",
  "actor_role": "cust-network-admin",
  "action_type": "peer_establish",
  "target_resource": "peer-86e1",
  "before_sha256": "9b1f...ae3",
  "after_sha256": "c12a...8f4",
  "evidence_refs": ["s3://cust-evidence/bundles/evt-20250910-7f2a.tgz#sig=..."],
  "operator_assertion": "verified-by-operator-ruiz:v1",
  "sampling_bucket": "medium",
  "truncated": false,
  "retention_class": "warm"
}
Notes: keep evidence_refs as signed URIs with short TTLs; do not embed full configs in the event unless sampling_bucket=full.
sample_log_lines:
Two sample log strategies to test in sandbox:
- Compact (preferred for constrained customers): include diffs as hashes only + evidence_refs. Log size ~ 1KB per event.
- Verbose (for initial onboarding/troubleshooting): include base64 gzipped before/after payloads in evidence_refs blob, not inline in JSON. Verbose events will be rate-limited and stored hot.
Example compact line (single NDJSON):
{"event_id":"evt-20250910-7f2b","timestamp_utc":"2025-09-10T18:22:31Z","actor_id":"system:orchestrator","action_type":"route_update","target_resource":"vpc-0a1b2c","before_sha256":"...","after_sha256":"...","evidence_refs":["https://evidence.redwood.internal/b/ev-7f2b?sig=..."],"sampling_bucket":"low"}
approval_flow:
Operator sandbox approval flow (staging):
1) Proposed change submitted via UI / CLI -> creates pending_event record and assigns event_id.
2) Auto-scan runs (syntax checks + quick diff hash). If match to known safe-policy -> auto-approve path, else human approval required.
3) Human approver views minimal evidence in UI (evidence_refs opened in separate signed viewer), verifies identity and signs assertion.
4) Approval writes operator_assertion and finalizes event. A signed compact receipt is produced and returned to customer for replay.
UX notes: the minimal view should render only: who, when, what changed (human-readable summary), and a single-click download of the evidence bundle. Avoid showing raw keys or long routing tables by default.
operator_playbook:
Operator steps to run the sandbox locally (macOS/Linux):
- Prereqs: python3.11, jq, docker. Clone repo: git clone github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-sandbox
- Start: make vpn-sim-start (starts local IPsec sim + small web UI).
- Create two simulated peer changes via CLI: ./sandboxctl propose peer up --peer-id=peer-test-1 --initiator=ops+ruiz@customer.com
- Observe NDJSON event written to ./sandbox/logs/events.ndjson and an evidence bundle under ./sandbox/evidence/evt-*.tgz
- Walk through UI approval flow, capture operator_assertion, and run ./sandboxctl verify-replay --event=evt-xxxx to validate signed receipt.
Troubleshooting: common failure is evidence upload to local S3 emulator failing on credentials; check .env.test and run minio locally.
sampling_strategy:
We suggest three buckets to balance audit fidelity vs bandwidth: low (hash-only, sample 1-in-100 routine changes), medium (hash + small meta, sample deterministic by tenant change-rate), full (include zipped before/after in evidence ref, used for initial onboarding or incident).
- Heuristics to force full: (a) change modifies NAT rules, (b) change touches edge peering, (c) user flagged by compliance.
- Sampling metadata must be part of the event so downstream auditors can explain omitted payloads. Keep sampling decisions deterministic (seeded by tenant-id + day) so replays are reproducible.
retention_and_storage:
Recommended defaults:
- hot: 7 days, full index, used for live rollback and onboarding.
- warm: 90 days, compact index (hashes + pointers), available for quick legal queries.
- cold: configurable up to 2 years (compressed archives, query-by-request).
Storage notes: evidence blobs should be sharded and TTL-signed; we must provide an export path for customers who want to keep evidence on their own S3/GCS. Cost controls: provide a toggle to cap verbose evidence uploads per month.
security_considerations:
- Events must be signed by the operator/service principal before being accepted into the immutable audit stream.
- Evidence URIs carry short-lived signatures (rotate every 24h).
- Redact secrets from bundles (private keys, shared secrets). The sandbox includes a redaction step that strips common key patterns.
- Provide an HSM-backed signing option for enterprise customers wanting maximum non-repudiation.
open_questions: Is a 24h signed-URI TTL acceptable for regulated customers in EU financial institutions? (legal asked about 72h)
Should we provide an optional third-party notarization step (e.g., sign-with-aws-kms-key owned by customer)?
How do we surface 'truncated=true' events in the Console so auditors don't miss context?
Do we need a separate schema for on-prem operator consoles that never touch Redwood-hosted evidence storage?
